transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-14 16:00 PDT | Duration: 45 mins | Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Nair (Redwood) — Markus Lee, Sofia Alvarez, Rajan Patel (CortexSearch)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, i m the AE, and with me is Priya our SE, um we'll run through our hosted API embeddings and rerank flow and then demo the console and quick sample code.
[00:18] Markus Lee: Hey thanks, yeah excited. Quick high level — we run site search across product catalog and docs, currently on Elastic + a homegrown reranker, relevance is shaky and costs are creeping up with increased vectors.
[00:33] Priya Nair: Got it. Can you share a little about scale? QPS, index size, latency SLOs?
[00:40] Sofia Alvarez: Sure, right now about 50 QPS at peak, ~12M docs, typical query latency budget is 200 to 300 ms end-to-end for UI, we can tolerate slightly above for long-tail.
[00:56] Rajan Patel: Most queries hit the top 5 results then we apply our reranker which is pretty heavy. We're looking for better relevance and lower per-query cost.
[01:10] Alex Chen: Makes sense. Quick qualification — are you open to hosted API for initial pilot or do you need VPC/on-prem from day one?
[01:18] Markus Lee: We'd prefer hosted to move fast but security will vet SOC2 and KMS integration. If hosted passes the compliance review we do a pilot, otherwise dedicated capacity in cloud.
[01:28] Priya Nair: Totally. Redwood's hosted offering is SOC2 compliant, we have customer KMS integrations and audit logs. We'll send the security pack after this call, it includes SOC2 report, encryption and KMS notes, and network options.
[01:40] Sofia Alvarez: Perfect.
[01:44] Priya Nair: Ok real quick architecture: we recommend an embedding + ANN vector store for retrieval, then a lightweight reranker call to our hosted rerank endpoint. That lets you keep recall high with efficient embed search and then only rerank the top N — that saves cost and latency.
[02:03] Rajan Patel: What's typical top-N? 10? 20?
[02:07] Priya Nair: Usually 10 to 50 depending on query length and latency SLO. For your 200-300 ms budget we'd demo top 10 rerank with a small model and show numbers.
[02:20] Alex Chen: I'll also mention caching — prefix/K-V cache can avoid re-computing for repeated similar queries, and batching helps throughput on the backend.
[02:31] Markus Lee: K-V cache? did you say K-V? we call it kv cache in-house, sometimes hyphenation gets spelled weird in transcripts.
[02:40] Priya Nair: Yeah sorry, K-V cache, but Redwood will manage prefix cache. Real world you see big wins on session-based patterns.
[02:50] Alex Chen: Alright, demo time — Priya will share her screen.
[03:00] [screen share starts] Priya Nair: Ok opening the Console — here is the embeddings tab, you can upload or index via API, see model choices. Quick note: we have curated open models and recommended profiles for embeddings — recommended for search is 'rwd-embed-small' or 'rwd-embed-512' depending on dimensionality.
[03:22] Sofia Alvarez: Are these Redwood-first models or off-the-shelf?
[03:26] Priya Nair: We surface curated open models and provide verified performance metrics — we also offer guidance on quantized variants for cost savings.
[03:36] Priya Nair: Now I'll demo the rerank endpoint — code snippet is on the right. You call /v1/rerank with original query, candidate docs, and we return scores and optionally transformed text.
[03:50] [00:03:50 Timestamp misread by auto-transcription] Rajan Patel: Does rerank run on same GPUs as embeddings or separate service?
[03:59] Priya Nair: In hosted we use model variants optimized for rerank; runtime will pick kernels and fallback depending on capacity. You can pin model versions if you need reproducible outputs.
[04:12] Alex Chen: Note on fallbacks: if a specific model is out of capacity we'll route to a compatible variant — value here is reliability.
[04:22] Markus Lee: Latency numbers please, ballpark for embed+ANN + rerank on top 10?
[04:29] Priya Nair: For typical medium sized models, retrieval+ANN ~30-80ms, rerank top 10 with a small rerank model ~50-120ms. So you can hit under 200ms end-to-end in many cases. We'll run benchmarks on your dataset to confirm.
[04:50] Sofia Alvarez: How do you compare cost to our current Elastic + custom reranker?
[04:56] Alex Chen: It depends — hosted has per-call and token economics; the Optimize toolkit will recommend batching and quantization to reduce per-token cost. For committed volume Dedicated often has better unit economics, we can run TCO.
[05:10] Rajan Patel: Any vector DB requirement? We currently use a local ANN.
[05:15] Priya Nair: You can keep your ANN, push embeddings to our hosted store, or use your ANN + call rerank. Many customers use Pinecone or Faiss; Redwood plays nicely with both patterns.
[05:29] Markus Lee: Ok, security again — can we get audit logs and per-route RBAC?
[05:35] Priya Nair: Yes, audit logs are available, plus role-based access in Console, SSO/SAML integrations for SSO, and customer-managed KMS options. We'll include the docs and a sample IAM policy.
[05:50] Alex Chen: Quick pointer to the docs link (shared in chat): https://redwood.ai/docs/hosted-api (note: auto transcription often mangles URL in the transcript).
[06:05] [Demo continues: live API call] Priya Nair: Running a sample: query "wireless earbuds battery life" — retrieval returned 12 candidates, rerank request with top 10, here's the response with scores, and we show improved top-1 relevance vs baseline.
[06:30] Sofia Alvarez: Looks promising, did you tune the prompt for rerank?
[06:35] Priya Nair: Yes, we use a structured prompt with fields for query, doc text, and optional signal weights. Console also surfaces recommended prompt templates.
[06:45] Rajan Patel: For evaluation, can we run A/B comparing current production vs Redwood rerank on same queries?
[06:51] Alex Chen: Absolutely — typical pilot is: you provide sample queries and labeled judgments or click logs, we run offline evals and online AB with shadow traffic.
[07:05] Markus Lee: How long for a pilot?
[07:08] Priya Nair: For an initial hosted smoke benchmark 2 days to get numbers, pilot with controlled traffic 2-4 weeks to gather metrics and adjust thresholds.
[07:20] Sofia Alvarez: Pricing model again?
[07:24] Alex Chen: Hosted per-token for rerank plus per-embedding unit for embeds. We'll share a sample pricing sheet and TCO comparison. If you commit to Dedicated there's reserved GPU pricing.
[07:35] [minor crosstalk]
[07:40] Rajan Patel: Any limits on payload size for rerank inputs?
[07:44] Priya Nair: We have recommended limits; extremely long docs are truncated or chunked. Best practice is to pass summarized or chunked text. We'll share the developer note.
[07:55] Markus Lee: Do you support stream responses for rerank or for chat only?
[08:00] Priya Nair: Streaming is supported for generation; rerank returns structured scores but can stream if you use a custom flow — again, we'll map to your use case.
[08:12] Alex Chen: Alright, let's capture risks: security lock (if hosted rejected, need dedicated), and accuracy/regression risk — Redwood has evals and regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[08:27] Priya Nair: We'll run a regression test suite and set up alerts if quality drops after model upgrades.
[08:35] Sofia Alvarez: Who owns latency SLO if hosted?
[08:38] Alex Chen: For hosted we provide regional SLOs and best-effort guarantees; for contractual SLAs and tighter latency we recommend Dedicated with committed capacity.
[08:50] Markus Lee: Good to know.
[08:55] [wrap up and recap] Alex Chen: Quick recap: Alex will send pricing, security pack and hosted vs dedicated TCO; Priya will prepare benchmark scripts and a sample rerank configuration; Markus will share datasets and queries. We agreed to schedule a pilot scoping call week of 2027-05-24.
[09:20] Sofia Alvarez: Thanks, this was very helpful.
[09:24] Rajan Patel: Thanks everyone.
[09:28] Alex Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links and docs.
[09:32] [call ends]

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcript had a few misheard words (VPC sometimes as V-B-C, K-V appeared as K V, URLs mangled). Speaker labels verified by AE after the call.

Shared artifacts: pricing spreadsheet (link sent in chat), security pack (SOC2 report, KMS notes), benchmark script (to be shared by Priya).

End of transcript.
